title: A guide to Old English pronunciation
authorization: User requested a practical Cook/Fulk pronunciation guide with American English cue words, minimal IPA, and help for sounds absent from American English.

placement.audience: Adult beginner; ordinary grammar terminology familiar; no prior Old English assumed

boundaries.existing_course: All eighteen unit contracts, learner/key masters, retained TeX/PDFs, cumulative registers and shared layout remain unchanged.

source_authorities.scope: Spelling, quantity, sounded clusters, front/back h articulation, doubled consonants, stress and exact one-sentence reading
Selected sound convention and its limits; vowel/diphthong values, contextual consonants and stress

resolved_convention.decision: Retain course spelling and quantity. Thorn/eth spellings do not encode voicing; hooked e/o retain the ordinary e/o sounds. Fulk example overpoints/underpoints may be removed only with the original and exact change recorded. Use eth for any normalized Fulk thorn example and record that change.

Use Fulk's long vowels, including held cat for long ash. Use traditional lax short e/i/o/u/y permitted in Fulk19 and compatible with Cook's practical table. Short/long pairs must have separate cues where their selected qualities differ; never claim duration is their only difference under these approximations.

Use father for a/ā, cat for æ/ǣ, bet for short e, bit for short i, foot for short u; use steady initial vowel of day/go for ē/ō and see/food for ī/ū. For short rounded o, qualify caught by whether the reader distinguishes cot/caught, and give an alternative mouth instruction. No r-coloured care, unqualified last/man, or whole day/go glide as an exact target.
Teach Fulk's more rounded short a in stressed syllables before m/n, using mann as the supplied example. Do not extend this stressed-vowel rule mechanically to every unstressed -an ending.

Choose Fulk20's rounded single-syllable ea/eo/ie convention, starting respectively as cat, the steady first vowel of day, and see, with one glide toward oo. Long spellings hold the first element longer. Distinguish this from Cook's actual table in a source endnote. Supply geong as an explicit non-diphthong exception.

Teach ordinary letters, c as k/ch, g as hard g/y/continuous voiced velar, usual sc as sh and cg as bridge, ordinary ng as finger with a supplied singe-type exception. State lexical and inflectional limits. cēlan, frosc and docga are supplied counterexamples, not a historical rule-generation test.

Give tongue/lip/airflow instructions for rounded y/ȳ, the back/front h sounds and continuous g. Use Cook's sounded h/w/c clusters without inventing a required voiceless-sonorant analysis, trill or aspiration rule. American r is a declared practical approximation. x/hs use the k+s classroom value supported by Cook; acknowledge Fulk's earlier x+s value only in the source note.

Adopt Fulk17: f/s/þ/ð ordinarily voiced between voiced sounds, voiceless word-initially/finally or beside a voiceless consonant. Teach voice with fan/van, sip/zip, thin/this. Supply hǣlðu and forðām as exceptions; qualify stress and word-part boundaries. Do not copy Cook's broader final-voicing rule or infer all sounds from modern cognates.

Keep vowel duration distinct from doubled-consonant duration and syllable weight. Retain audible, differentiated unstressed endings. Give ordinary first/root stress with ge-/be-/for- and verb-prefix limits; supply anginne as stress on ginn and gescēop on scēop. Use printed length for careful exercises, explaining briefly that unstressed function words/prefixes could shorten in connected speech.

example_policy.word_meanings: Visible wherever needed for a task; no memorization required
example_policy.forms: Use selected source examples or existing image-audited course forms; exact source and pronunciation application recorded separately
example_policy.normalization: Removing Fulk teaching dots or changing þ to ð is declared per form. No inferred macrons, silent dialect conversion or general respelling.
example_policy.stress_aids: Bold and optional dividing hyphens are visibly declared reading aids, not source spelling
example_policy.additional_examples: Require a bounded evidence-backed contract amendment before they enter assessed tasks

selected_reading.line_convention: First prose line; no invented printed line number
selected_reading.text: On anginne gescēop God heofonan and eorðan.
selected_reading.supplied_translation: In the beginning God created heaven and earth.
selected_reading.purpose: Supported oral reading and sound observations only
local_support: gescēop g/sc, root stress and long ēo
heofonan three syllables, eo and voiced f
eorðan two syllables, eo and voiced ð
selected_reading.normalization: Source note cues 1–3 omitted from the learner excerpt; words and punctuation retained. The original notes remain in the cited source transcription; this guide supplies all meaning and pronunciation support without assigning those grammar questions.

practice.prompt_type: Read four pairs and identify the long vowel in each
Give the taught sound or mouth instruction for the indicated letters, then read the supplied word
Identify voicing of the indicated letter and explain the context or supplied exception
Give syllable count and stressed syllable; identify a doubled consonant where present
Read the fully supported Cook sentence and answer three sound questions

learner_design.language: Terse original exposition; no prior OE assumed
learner_design.ipa: At most one first-introduction occurrence for each unfamiliar sound where useful; no full-word IPA and no transcription tasks. Prefer ordinary words and mouth instructions.
learner_design.american_cues: Specify only the relevant part of the English word; distinguish an approximation from an exact equivalence.
learner_design.notes: Source disagreements, section locators and normalization details belong in endnotes/editorial evidence.
learner_design.tables: Shared Cambria 10.5-point booktabs style with compact readable panels
